ignore.reason: MCP SDK DNS rebinding vulnerability - not applicable as SDKs are used in controlled environments, not exposed to untrusted network requests
Rake OS command injection - not applicable as rake is only used as a development/build dependency, not processing untrusted input

JSONPath prototype pollution - not exploitable as jsonpath queries are generated by the SDK at build time, not from untrusted user input. No patched version available; users can migrate to jsonpath-rfc9535 by setting Jsonpath config to 'rfc9535'

JSONPath arbitrary code injection via unsafe evaluation - not exploitable as jsonpath queries are generated by the SDK at build time, not from untrusted user input. No patched version available; users can migrate to jsonpath-rfc9535 by setting Jsonpath config to 'rfc9535'

qs.stringify DoS on null/undefined comma-format array entries with encodeValuesOnly - not reachable as qs is a transitive dep of express/body-parser, which only call qs.parse, never the vulnerable stringify path

Path traversal in serve-static on Windows - not reachable as the generated MCP server never uses serveStatic from @hono/node-server. Fix requires a 1.x -> 2.x major bump of the runtime server adapter; revisit when upgrading the hono stack

Arbitrary file read via esbuild dev server on Windows - not reachable as esbuild is only invoked for build-time bundling, never in --serve mode. Fix (0.28.1) is outside the ^0.27.0 range required by @gram-ai/functions and wrangler, so it cannot be overridden without violating parent constraints

x/crypto/openpgp is unmaintained by design and the advisory has no fixed version, so no bump can ever clear it. Not reachable: the generated Terraform provider does not import any golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp packages; x/crypto is only a transitive dep of the Terraform plugin stack
